newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pare losses late, end 2.35 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pare losses late, end 2.35 pct lower.

text.p: Thai stocks ended 2.35 percent lower on Thursday as late buying by local funds failed to fully reverse earlier losses caused by sales of blue-chip stocks on currency concerns, traders said.

The composite SET index ended the day down 13.43 points, or 2.35 percent, at 557.87. The SET 50 blue chip index ended 1.22 points, or 2.93 percent, lower at 40.40. Turnover was a moderate 6.62 billion baht.
The market now stands at its lowest level since May 1989.
Local funds, encouraged by renewed currency stability and a pledge of support from the Bank of Japan, went bargain hunting in the afternoon, traders said.
"The currency was better in the afternoon, the news that the Bank of Japan may help to maintain the baht helped," said a trader at General Finance and Securities.
Foreign investors, spooked by Wednesday's heavy speculative assault on the Thai baht, unloaded blue chips throughout the day, brokers said.

"I think some local funds came in the afternoon but the trend is still for the foreigners to sell and there was big pressure on stocks like Bangkok Bank and Siam Cement throughout the day," said a local broker.
Reported currency intervention by regional central banks and a calmer money market had not yet convinced all foreigners to hold their positions, said one local trader.

"Some clients believe there is a lot of talk and you do wonder how much these banks have to spend in the market to claim they are intervening. That said you might think we are due for a small technical correction tommorrow," he said.
A busy day of results had a limited impact on the overall market which was dominated by currency concerns, brokers added.

"The market was almost entirely sentiment driven today. You might believe that Thai Telephone's (results) weren't as bad as expected, but quite frankly the market is so bad at the moment that no more bad news is good news," said a trader at Krungthai Thanakit.
Bangkok Bank Plc BBl.BK shed six to 150, Siam Cement Plc lost 38 to 520, and Thai Farmers Bank Plc was off two to 98.
